Design sheet · admin provider setup · task C

Price on request

Many services the team sets up have no price yet. They now go live anyway. Customers see “Price on request” (never “Get a quote”, never $0) and can Ask for price — a chat with that business, already typed — or Call when the business has a phone. They can’t be put in the cart or booked online until the business adds a price. Providers and the team pick a fourth choice, “No price yet”, when they add a service, and see a gentle reminder to add a price later. Every frame below is drawn from the real screen it changes; the file it mirrors is named under each one.

1Search results2Category page3Provider page4Not taken over yet5Service page6Ask for price7Cart8Customer web states9Customer phone app10Provider web11Provider phone app12Admin web + phone13Words

1Search results Customer web

A service with no price now shows up in search. Its price line reads Price on request in the same quiet grey the card already uses for “no figure”. The card keeps its Call button (only when the business has a phone) and the green arrow into the service page, where Ask for price is the main button. A no-price card never shows an offer band, a visit-fee flag or a “total at checkout” line — those describe a total that does not exist. Card 3 is a business the team set up that has not taken over yet: Phone only, so no arrow.

Price filters and sorts: a “price from / to” filter leaves no-price services out, and “Price: Low to High” / “High to Low” put them last — the order of everything else does not change (PLAN C10).

2Category and city pages Customer web

These cards are businesses, not services. They show From CA$… only when the business has at least one priced service; a business whose services are all Price on request simply has no price line — the card never guesses one. The three buttons stay exactly as they are today: View profile (green), Message, and Call only when there is a phone.

The second card (green outline = how the real card looks on hover) is Joe's Plumbing, whose services are all Price on request: no price line at all — exactly today’s rule. The landing lines “everyone starts at…” and “real prices” skip such businesses (PLAN C11).

3Provider page — the services list Customer web

On the business’s own page, a no-price service reads Price on request in the same bold ink as a real price. Where a priced service has Book Now, it has Ask for price: one tap opens a chat with Joe's Plumbing with “Hi, what's the price for Water heater install?” already typed. The existing Call button stays exactly as it is, and only appears when the business has a phone. No cart button — it cannot be booked online.

No offer pill and no “View offer” on a no-price row — an offer takes money off a price that does not exist (PLAN C11). The row keeps its photo, name link and “At home / At provider’s location” badges.

4A business the team set up that hasn’t taken over yet Customer web

Until the owner takes the profile over, online booking is off. The page already says so with the existing amber notice — “Online booking not available. This provider doesn't accept online bookings. Please tap the Call button to book any service.” — and every row shows Call only. Nothing new is added here; the no-price row simply looks like every other row on this page.

5Service page Customer web

The price box says Price on request with one plain line under it in the page’s existing blue note style. Ask for price takes the green spot where Book now sits on a priced service; Message and Call stay as they are. On phone and iPad the sticky bar at the bottom carries Call + Ask for price.

6“Ask for price” opens a chat, already typed Customer web

Same flow as today’s button: signed in, it opens the conversation with that business and fills the box with “Hi, what's the price for Water heater install?” — the customer can edit it and press send. Signed out, it goes to the existing sign-in page and comes back here afterwards. Nothing is sent until they press send.

7Cart: a service that lost its price Customer web

If a service in someone’s cart has no price any more, checkout takes it out and says so in one clear line, with a way to ask for the price instead. Everything else in the cart carries on as normal.

If the removed service was the only one for that business, the business disappears from the cart and the same line shows above the empty cart. Bookings already made keep their price (PLAN C12).

8Customer web — every other state Customer web · phone width

Loading uses the search page’s real skeleton. After sending, the message shows Sent; if sending fails or the phone is offline, the existing red Retry pill appears on the message. A business with no phone simply has no Call button anywhere — Ask for price is the only action.

9Customer phone app clinqetmobileuserapp

Same rules as the web, drawn in the app’s own style (system font, its StyleSheet values). Ask for price goes straight into the existing chat screen with the message typed and the keyboard up, with a light haptic tap. Online booking off → the existing amber banner and Call only.

10Provider web — the service form and the services list clinqetwebpartnerapp

The cost-type pills get a fourth choice, No price yet. Picking it hides the price box and shows one reminder in the form’s existing blue hint style. In the services list a no-price service shows a Price on request pill and an Add a price link that opens the same form. An amount of 0 is refused — “no price” is its own choice.

Drawn side by side so both changes are visible in one frame; in the app the form slides in as the existing right-hand drawer (max-w-lg, dark backdrop) and is full-screen on a phone. Price 0 refused: the price box shows its existing red error, “Enter a price above 0, or choose No price yet.” The old line “Services without a price won’t appear in search results” is removed (PLAN C9).

11Provider phone app clinqetmobilepartnerapp

The same fourth chip, wrapping onto a second line on a narrow phone. The services list gets the pill and Add a price; long-press a service for quick actions (with a light haptic), and pull down to refresh.
